statement: For delta<=1/4 and delta sqrt(2G)<=1/4, channel Cauchy-Schwarz gives |<u,B_t v>|<=delta sqrt(2G E(u)E(v)) for pi u=0 and |<1,B_t v>|<=delta sqrt(2A E(v)). Nonreversible nominal invariance gives d||h-1||2^2/dt<=-||h-1||2^2/C_P+4delta^2 A, hence ||h_t-1||2^2<=exp(-t/C_P)||h0-1||2^2+4C_P delta^2 A. Put B=max(1,A/a0); additionally delta^2<=epsilon^2/(16C_P A B) and rational T>=C_P[log(1/pi(u))+log(2B/epsilon^2)] give EVERY t>=T whole TV<=epsilon/2 and each ABSOLUTE first-mean error<=epsilon from point population u. Point-mass density is in L2(pi). For conditional Poisson, log(1/pi(u))<=sum lambda+sum[log(u_i!)-u_i log lambda_i]; ordinary rational polynomial upper bounds yield fixed-R polynomial numerical T,delta^-1 and binary arithmetic. The actual law tracks a fixed pi tube; no invariant law for nonautonomous Q_t or exact convergence at nonzero errors is claimed.
